Ontology_AssayAndWorkflow_prompt.notes: The study uses two proteomics approaches: a global quantitative analysis of retinal explants and a targeted affinity purification (co-IP) using a biotinylated CDR1 peptide. Both were analyzed using DDA (Top 5) on an LTQ Orbitrap XL and quantified via MaxQuant intensity (LFQ). While Western Blots were used for phosphorylation and histone acetylation, the MS search parameters only listed N-terminal acetylation and oxidation as variable modifications, not site-specific PTM enrichment for the MS runs.

organism: retina organ culture was prepared from freshly removed eye bulbs of the house swine (Sus scrofa domestica Linnaeus, 1758)

The reviewed SwissProt databases with the taxonomies Homo sapiens (date: 13 April 2021, number of sequences: 20,408) and Sus scrofa (date: 13 April 2021, number of sequences: 1,439) were used for protein identifications and quantification.
cell_types: progressive loss of retinal ganglion cells (RGCs)
noncellular_sources: biomarker candidate in the serum of glaucoma patients
scope: MS-based co-immunoprecipitation experiments confirmed the specific interaction of synthetic CDR1 with retinal acidic leucine-rich nuclear phosphoprotein 32A
we immobilized the synthetic CDR1 peptide on magnetic beads by biotin-streptavidin conjugation and performed a protein enrichment from retinal protein homogenate
the eluate fractions of both bead groups (CTRL and CDR1) were subjected to further proteomic MS analysis

Ontology_SampleSourceAndScope_prompt.notes: The study performed two types of MS analyses: 1) affinity purification (co-IP) using biotinylated CDR1 peptides to capture ANP32A, and 2) quantitative proteomics on retinal explants. Per precedence rules, the affinity-purified material (co-IP) defines the sample_scope as 'purified protein or complex'. Mixed species flag is true because the human database was used to supplement the swine database for identification.
